# Equality in the planar three-cap overlap inequality

Let K be a planar convex body of area V. Let three closed halfplanes cover
K, and let A_i be their areas in K. Assume A_i>0 for every i. Then

    A_1+A_2+A_3-V = (3/4) min_i A_i                     (1)

holds if and only if K is a triangle and, up to permutation, the three
halfplanes are its vertex caps bounded by the lines parallel to the opposite
sides through the triangle centroid. In that case every A_i=4V/9.

The inequality and its arbitrary-cover scope are proved in
`candidate e239a5fb0d0efe4d` and
`candidate 79c19cddb83423ea`.
The only additional input here is the equality classification proved at the
end of `candidate c22519c29667168e`: a noncollinear
stationary centered-chord triple with positive balanced weights has weighted
cap average 4/9 only for the triangle-centroid configuration, and its
balanced weights are all 1/3. Opposite pairs and half-weight degeneracies
instead have average 1/2.

## Proof

Write r=3/4 and F(A)=sum_i A_i-r min_i A_i. If two of the halfplanes
cover K, and i is the remaining index, then

    F(A)>=V+A_i-r min_j A_j>=V+(1-r)min_j A_j>V.

Consequently equality excludes a two-cap subcover. The arbitrary-cover
reduction in the second source shows that the three halfplanes cover the
whole plane and their normals form a strictly positive rank-two circuit.

Tighten all three offsets to their common concurrence point as in Section 5
of the first source, giving cap areas A_i'<=A_i. Put delta_i=A_i-A_i'.
Coordinatewise monotonicity gives the stronger quantitative estimate

    F(A)-F(A') >= (1-r)sum_i delta_i.

Indeed min A-min A'<=max_i delta_i<=sum_i delta_i. The proved inequality
F(A')>=V, together with (1), forces every delta_i=0 and F(A')=V. In
particular every A_i'>0.

The concurrent equality parameters are global minimizers in the compact
problem of Section 4 of the first source. They cannot have a boundary
concurrence point or an opposite normal pair, because the same strict
two-cap argument applies. They therefore have an interior concurrence point
y, proper cuts, and a nondegenerate positive normal triangle. The tied-min
stationarity proof supplies t_i>=0, sum t_i=1, supported on the minimum
caps, such that

    alpha_i=1-(3/4)t_i>0,
    sum alpha_i=9/4,
    sum alpha_i S_i u_i=0,

and every chord has midpoint y. Moreover

    sum_i [alpha_i/(9/4)] A_i' = F(A')/(9/4) = (4/9)V.

The archived planar equality classification now forces K to be a triangle
with these chords its canonical centroid chords, and forces
alpha_i/(9/4)=1/3 for each i. Thus alpha_i=3/4, t_i=1/3, all three
indices are active minima, and all three cap areas equal 4V/9.

Finally the tightening changed every original offset by the same positive
amount if the original concurrence deficit B was strictly negative. In
the triangle-centroid configuration every tightened cut passes through
int(K), so decreasing its threshold by any positive amount adds positive
area: a small disk at an interior point of the cut contains a positive-area
strip of the enlarged cap. This contradicts delta_i=0. Hence B=0, and the
original caps were already the same concurrent canonical caps.

Conversely those three caps each have area 4V/9, cover the whole plane,
and have total excess V/3=(3/4)(4V/9), proving (1).

## Zero-area qualification

The positivity assumption is necessary for this rigidity conclusion. If
one cap has area zero, equality in the overlap inequality merely says the
other two form an almost-everywhere disjoint cover of K. Many convex bodies
admit such a pair of complementary cuts, so triangle rigidity is false in
that case. No assertion of triangle rigidity is used on zero-minimum fibers.

This is an equality classification for an ordinary planar local theorem.
It gives no sign for the remaining mixed-fiber dispersion/cross-capture
quantity in Section 6 of the first source.
